thread:
devon: FYI I ran dependency scan on edge-infer and cve-bot flagged a legacy Windows crypto DLL used by our model loader: CVE-2026-1829. CVSS 7.5.

cve-bot: Automated scan: edge-infer@main -> dependency 'legacy-crypto.dll' matched CVE-2026-1829 (high). See: https://cve.example/CVE-2026-1829

maria: quick summary for context? what does the vuln allow?

devon: Short: improper validation in legacy-crypto.dll can lead to unauthenticated signature forgery in certain RSA chains if attacker can provide a crafted WASM plugin or model bundle. Exploit requires uploading a model artifact to our model-store (S3).

samir: Can the artifact upload flow be exploited externally? We require auth on the bucket and presigned URLs, but older edge services still accept unsigned uploads from deploy pipeline.

devon: Right — current risk path: compromised CI runner or a pipeline that can push to the old uploads endpoint. New pipelines use signed uploads, but a few demo runners are still on legacy flow (edge-infer-demo-runner).

irene: TL;DR: plausible but not trivial. What's the immediate ask? patch, block, or exception? :eyes:

devon: Proposed remediation plan: 1) short-term compensating controls + temporary scanning exception for deployments for 14 days while infra team patches demos. 2) restrict upload endpoint by IP and require signed URLs. 3) rotate KMS keys used to sign model bundles and enable audit logging to SIEM. 4) schedule patch of legacy-crypto.dll in next weekly maintenance window.

maria: Do we have tests that will catch signature-forgery if someone exploits? If not, we should add an eval prompt set to detect tampered-models before rolling out.

samir: Ops note: we can add a WAF rule to block suspicious multipart uploads and lock the legacy endpoint with a deny-by-default rule. Also can disable the demo runners immediately.

tony: CI impact: current PRs will block due to policy enforcement. If we apply a temporary override in the policy store, we should add gating checks (IP restriction + KMS rotation) before allowing override.

devon: I pushed a draft compensating-controls doc in the ticket with exact steps and links. Excerpt: ```Compensating controls: - Disable legacy demo upload endpoint (edge-infer-demo) - Apply WAF signature for multipart anomaly - Enforce signed S3 uploads for all new pipelines - KMS rotate model-signing key + revoke old key - Route model validation through static verifier before loading - Enable audit log stream to SIEM and alert on model-signing failures```

irene: I want explicit timelines and an owner for each item. If we accept a temporary allowlist for the scan false positive, it must be limited to 14 days and revoked earlier if patch lands. Also require periodic audit (every 48h) check-in from devon.

devon: Owners: - disable endpoint: samir (today) - WAF rule: tony (today) - enforce signed uploads: infra team / maria (3 days) - KMS rotation: maria (2 days) - patch dependency: eng-runtime (weekly window in 7 days) - audit alerts: samir (1 day)

samir: I disabled the demo runner and put a deny rule behind a feature flag. Will monitor for false positives.

irene: Approval: I approve a temporary scan allowlist for edge-infer artifacts on the condition that the compensating controls listed are implemented and evidence posted in the ticket. 14-day max. devon to post verification logs every 48h.

devon: Noted. I'll attach SIEM alerts and presigned URL audit to the ticket. Planning to patch codebase Friday maintenance slot.

deploy-bot: deploy attempted for edge-infer PR#412 -> blocked by policy (high severity CVE) (override pending).

tony: I'll file the override request with the required evidence links now.

maria: For record, QA will add an evaluation harness to detect forged model bundles. ETA 4 days.

irene: Thanks all. If patch completes early revoke the allowlist immediately. Otherwise we'll re-evaluate at the 7-day mark. :white_check_mark:
